newsitem.title: USA: Clinton resumes weekly meeting with economic aides.
newsitem.headline: Clinton resumes weekly meeting with economic aides.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday resumed a series of weekly meetings with economic advisers that was interrupted to await Janet Yellen's confirmation as chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, a spokesman said. White House press secretary Mike McCurry said the purpose of the meeting was "just to take a look at the general lay of the land in macro-economic terms."

Asked if any new concerns about the economy prompted resumption of the meetings, McCurry said: "No, just a desire to keep looking carefully at the overall trend of the economy, which we believe is sound and strong."

He said participants in the meeting, besides Clinton and Yellen, were Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, National Economic Adviser Gene Sperling and other members of the CEA.
